newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth sees higher 1997 cash cap spending.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth sees higher 1997 cash cap spending.

text.p: Retail giant Woolworth Corp said Wednesday it foresaw its cash capital spending reaching $285 million in 1997, more than double the $134 million spent the previous year.
Woolworth said it would be spending more money to finance a plan to open new stores and remodel old ones.
It also planned to invest money in infrastructure and "strategic" acquisitions.
"The company expects the primary impact of the new store growth to take place during the second half of 1997," it said.

Woolworth said it expected to open 400 new stores, 250 of which will be in the Athletic Group formats. It said it planned to remodel or relocate about 500 stores, about 300 of them in the Athletic format.
"Substantial new store openings and remodelings are also planned for the various formats in the Northern Group of apparel stores in the United States and Canada," it said.
Some Woolworth general merchandise stores, Kinney shoe chain stores and After Thoughts jewelry chain stores will also undergo remodeling.
Woolworth said it planned to seek strategic acquisitions, "like the recent purchase of the Eastbay catalog operation, a combination that provides real benefits for both businesses."
It bought the operation for $140 million plus $6 million that become payable if certain post-closing performance targets are achieved.

Woolworth said it would improve its infrastructure by installing new systems and equipment at four service centers, reorganizing its accounting centers and strengthening its real estate organizations and merchandise planning and analysis functions.
The retail giant reported a fourth-quarter profit of $0.74 against a loss of $0.80 for the same period last year. The fourth quarter and full fiscal year ended January 25, 1997.
